concepts.title: Functions and Their Evaluation
concepts.definition: A function pairs every admissible input with exactly one output through a stated rule; combining two functions pointwise gives new functions for sum, difference, product and quotient, each evaluated by substituting the same input into both rules.
concepts.key_idea: One input, one output; a vertical line may cross the graph only once.

concepts.title: Domain and Range of a Function
concepts.definition: The domain lists every input a function accepts, either stated openly or implied by the rule, while the range collects every output the rule can actually produce; a square root rejects inputs below its cut-off and never returns a negative value.
concepts.formula: domain = inputs where the rule makes sense
concepts.key_idea: Refuse inputs that break the rule; the outputs never leave the range set.

concepts.title: Types of Functions
concepts.definition: Familiar function families include polynomials ranked by their highest power, quotients of polynomials, exponentials with a fixed base, logarithms as their inverses, the step-like greatest integer map, the absolute value map and the three-valued sign map.
concepts.key_idea: Name the family from the shape of the rule; degree reads off the top power.

concepts.title: Limits by Substitution and Cancellation
concepts.definition: The limit of a function at a point records the output the rule approaches; well-behaved rules settle by direct substitution, while a zero-over-zero form is first simplified by cancelling the vanishing factor and then substituted.
concepts.formula: poly = c + b * x + a * sq
concepts.key_idea: Substitute when it works; cancel the common factor when it does not.

concepts.title: Continuity of a Function at a Point
concepts.definition: A function is continuous at a point when the approach from the left, the approach from the right and the actual value all agree there; a mismatch between the two one-sided approaches breaks the limit and marks a jump.
concepts.key_idea: Three numbers must match: left approach, right approach, actual value.

concepts.title: Average and Instantaneous Rate of Change
concepts.definition: Dividing a change in one quantity by the change in another gives an average rate, while shrinking the interval to a point yields the instantaneous rate; for a volume growing like a square of time, that instantaneous rate itself grows linearly with time.
concepts.key_idea: Average rate uses a real interval; instantaneous rate is its limiting slope.

concepts.title: Derivative of a Polynomial by the Power Rule
concepts.definition: Differentiation measures how fast a function changes; the power rule drops each exponent by one and uses the old exponent as a multiplier, and a sum of terms differentiates term by term.
concepts.key_idea: x^n turns into n x^(n-1); constants die and lines keep their slope.

concepts.title: Chain Rule for Composite Functions
concepts.definition: A composite function wraps one rule inside another; its derivative multiplies the outer derivative, taken at the inner value, by the inner derivative, so a shifted cube like a linear term cubed differentiates to fifteen times the square of the inner expression.
concepts.key_idea: Differentiate outside, keep inside untouched, then multiply by the inside derivative.

concepts.title: Tangent Line to a Curve
concepts.definition: The tangent at a point of a curve touches it there with slope equal to the derivative; evaluating the rule at the contact point gives the height, and the point-slope form assembles the tangent equation.
concepts.key_idea: Slope from the derivative, height from the rule, then point-slope does the rest.
